student_action: Move the existing display assignment between _ready and _process; predict the reading before restarting.
visible_consequence: One reading stays fixed; repeated readings continue changing while the same museum remains active.
useful_contrast: Same instruction and display, different invocation timing.
image_reason: The counter is large and readable, with enough room context to locate it.
image_cannot_prove: A still showing 118 cannot establish whether the number updates, or how often the callback runs.
proposal: Proposed comparison beside the photograph: three labelled instants, with a fixed reading in the _ready row and changing readings in the _process row. Mark them as illustrative values, not recorded frames. Put the same assignment beside both rows.
flags: The display is supplied; do not imply the student builds a new counter.
No timer metaphor or new three-dimensional object is needed.

student_action: Change the centre, then change the shared radius, then change only the collision radius in separate source edits.
visible_consequence: The point moves; the visible sphere grows; a collision-only change changes where locomotion stops while the surface stays fixed.
useful_contrast: A Vector3 or float value is distinct from the object receiving it; mesh and collision can receive the same radius independently.
image_reason: The corridor includes the sphere conditions and their separate stations.
image_cannot_prove: Visibility does not establish a collider, physical stopping distance, variable type or reference identity.
proposal: Proposed two-panel diagram: one numeric radius feeds a drawn circle and a dashed collision boundary; then only the dashed boundary changes. A tiny adjacent call chain, SphereMesh.new() → sphere reference → body.mesh, names the actual programming relation. Label the dashed boundary as an explanatory drawing.
flags: Do not label the empty station from its position in this photograph without checking the source layout.
CENTRE is currently a constant edited before rerun, not a live draggable variable.
Collision constrains virtual locomotion; the photograph does not show headset or hand resistance.

student_action: Hold the existing point and move along one named axis; compare its position readout before and after release.
visible_consequence: The held object changes position while the reporting cards and coordinate frame remain in place.
useful_contrast: One retained object reference, repeatedly read position values; world and named local frames can report different numbers for the same place.
image_reason: The coloured axes, point and paired coordinate cards appear together.
image_cannot_prove: The still cannot show grabbing, scope across callbacks, or which temporary values survive an update.
proposal: Proposed margin strip with two successive reads: the same pt reference points to the same body; each read obtains a new Vector3 value. Highlight only Y for an upward move. State the chosen frame; do not place invented readings onto the photographed cards.
flags: The actual reporting frame is scaled; local coordinates are not simply world coordinates with another origin.
The point and hold connection are supplied; scope should be shown by a small code/value strip rather than an invented room metaphor.

student_action: Move an endpoint, then compare two endpoint pairs with equal distance but different direction; reverse the subtraction.
visible_consequence: The segment turns or changes length; reversing the computed displacement reverses its direction without changing the endpoint separation.
useful_contrast: Vector3 displacement versus float distance; a return value versus its supplied drawing.
image_reason: The isolated endpoints and joining line are visually simple.
image_cannot_prove: The dark readouts are not evidence of the numeric result, and a line alone has no labelled direction.
proposal: Proposed comparison of a horizontal and vertical pair, both 1.5 m apart: b-a → Vector3, then length() → 1.5. Add a reversed arrow in a third small view while leaving endpoints fixed. Keep the arrow explicitly diagrammatic.
flags: Do not infer a changed museum arrow from the photographed undirected segment.
Coincident endpoints supply a useful zero case; no normalization lesson is needed here.

student_action: Move, pause and return with the pen; predict whether each reading enters the record, then join the retained neighbours in order.
visible_consequence: Accepted samples remain as a route after the point has moved away. A pause contributes no new position under the distance rule.
useful_contrast: Frames still occur while the list stays unchanged; a for traversal visits retained entries within one update.
image_reason: The clean-hall view shows the three recording stations, their lines and data displays; it is substantially stronger than the broad room view.
image_cannot_prove: Displayed paths do not prove they are a student's drawing, reveal acceptance thresholds, or establish the starter companion's persistence behavior.
proposal: Three proposed diagram beats: append a named point to slots 0,1,2; a distance comparison gives true/false and either appends or keeps the list; a moving highlight visits pairs 0–1 and 1–2. Use an explicit small illustrative record, not invented values pasted onto the museum monitor.
flags: Prefer Point_Trace-2.webp; the first route image gives little evidence of the recorder.
Reconcile museum nib/snapping/session storage with the starter's centre sampling and persistent local file before asserting exact values.
Avoid showing a while loop waiting for motion; the real introductory comparison is checked once per frame.

student_action: Release a trace, inspect its fitted display and rounded addresses, then find separate list entries that share a displayed address.
visible_consequence: The original ordered record stays distinct while the derived drawing gains repeated grid addresses and straightened joins.
useful_contrast: List index versus spatial address; source record versus derived display.
image_kind: Saved museum context capture; weak concept evidence
image_reason: The clear route image locates the hall but concentrates on neighbouring figures, not the trace-to-grid operation. The second image is an obstructed doorway and should not be selected.
image_cannot_prove: Neither route capture shows the relevant source/rounded trace comparison or preservation of the source list.
proposal: Proposed comparison must carry the teaching: a small ordered list with indices 0,1,2,3 → fit/resize → XYZ rounding. Show two indices reaching one grid address while the original list remains visible. Use the photograph only as a small location image, or flag the missing focused capture.
flags: Do not treat the mannequins as visual metaphors for list entries.
Use museum fit-then-round order; the starter rounds original values before fitting.
Session transfer is not persistence across project restarts.

student_action: Choose three non-collinear positions, join their boundary, then submit the face in a stated order.
visible_consequence: The same corners support points, an outline or a filled surface according to the operation requested.
useful_contrast: Stored positions stay fixed while the renderer receives a different instruction.
image_reason: The existing board already compares points, boundary and face beside the spatial work.
image_cannot_prove: The still cannot show the source list, a live submission call, or what reversing winding would do under the material's culling policy.
proposal: Small proposed ordered-index strip [0,1,2] aligned with the board's three corners. Reuse the existing points/outline/face comparison instead of inventing another scene.
flags: The starter face material is two-sided. Do not promise that reversing corner order makes its face disappear.
If winding is illustrated, label an explicitly one-sided comparison and show its viewing direction.

student_action: Read a face's three indices, close one missing face, then change a shared corner.
visible_consequence: An opening closes; every face referring to the edited position changes together.
useful_contrast: One position list with multiple references to its indices; changing a position differs from changing connectivity.
image_reason: The close view of the existing open/closed boundary board is stronger than the general hall view.
image_cannot_prove: A closed picture does not demonstrate a collider or show the underlying face-index list.
proposal: Proposed margin diagram: four numbered positions, three short face rows, then the added row highlighted. Highlight the same corner number in every referring row before showing its changed position.
flags: Index references into a data list are not object aliasing; name that distinction.
The photograph includes a billboard diagram, not evidence that the learner has operated a new mesh editor.

student_action: Move one corner out of the face plane, predict affected triangles, then compare the alternative diagonal.
visible_consequence: Shared coordinates deform connected faces; the diagonal determines which triangular patch spans each part.
useful_contrast: Same connections with a changed vertex, then same vertices with changed connections.
image_kind: Saved museum capture outside the current route's selected pair
image_reason: The existing teaching plate is readable. Current route images show the prefab shelf and miss the main shared-corner concept.
image_cannot_prove: This is a photograph of an explanatory plate, not a before/after recording of a learner moving a corner.
supporting_figure_kind: Existing authored diagram, not a runtime capture
proposal: Reuse the existing numbered two-state diagram at a readable size and identify it as a diagram. A tiny proposed third panel can compare [4,5,7]/[5,6,7] with [4,5,6]/[4,6,7] under the same displaced corner.
flags: Do not present the prefab library photograph as proof of shared mesh-data editing.
Changing one vertex is not moving the entire node.

student_action: Call the same position generator with two radii; predict both returned lists before comparing the resulting forms.
visible_consequence: Opposite pairs retain their relation while their distances from the centre change.
useful_contrast: One function definition, two calls and two data results; editing a generated result does not change its generating rule.
image_kind: Saved museum context capture; weak concept evidence
image_reason: The doorway and solids locate the encounter, but do not show the reduced generator or its two calls.
image_cannot_prove: A courtyard of forms cannot show parameters, local values, return behavior or whether a function runs once or every frame.
proposal: Proposed comparison: octahedron_positions(0.5) → six positions → small octahedron; octahedron_positions(0.8) → six positions → larger octahedron. Keep one short shared function label above both. Do not depict a function as a physical factory in the museum.
flags: The nearby sphere resolution figure is a useful existing geometry comparison, but does not demonstrate an authored returning function.
Keep trigonometry and mesh assembly supplied.

student_action: In the proposed small edit study, create two familiar mesh resources with different settings and assign each to its displaying node.
visible_consequence: Changing one separately created resource changes its displayed geometry while the other remains unchanged.
useful_contrast: Class name, created resource, displaying node and supplied scene have separate roles.
image_reason: The entry view shows more labelled library specimens than the inside view.
image_cannot_prove: Fixed library specimens do not expose object references or prove independent live editing; several dark surfaces are hard to read.
proposal: Proposed flat reference diagram beside the photo: SphereMesh.new() twice gives resource A and resource B; each feeds one node's mesh property. Highlight only A's radius edit. Keep this separate from the photographed library.
flags: A universal parameter editor is not installed in this hall.
Authored classes remain a later Colour lesson; this is use of an existing engine class.

student_action: Inspect the controlled first row, then use the reduced column function to change one radius, height or side count while holding the other inputs fixed.
visible_consequence: A profile edit changes the silhouette; height changes vertical spacing; side count changes the polygonal cross-section.
useful_contrast: Independent inputs to one rule; outer loop over profile rings and inner loop around each ring.
image_reason: The front row and aisle are legible; the inside alternative contains a large diagonal visual obstruction and mixes varied families.
image_cannot_prove: The photograph alone does not verify held inputs or show the two loops. Later rows vary shape and height as well as sampling.
proposal: Proposed diagram with a vertical radius list and one highlighted ring; a short row of 4/6/8/12/16-sided cross-sections keeps radius fixed. A second small line states rings × sides = position count for the reduced study. Avoid marking every museum specimen as a controlled trial.
flags: Museum specimens are fixed; the learner edit belongs to a proposed host.
Reduced study profile intervals are straight; museum sections are curved.
The image is strong evidence of faceting, not of live parameter controls.

student_action: Compare the flat O profile with its passage and vessel uses; predict what changes when route or section scale changes while the outline stays fixed.
visible_consequence: The same outline can yield visibly different spatial forms through different construction choices.
useful_contrast: Source data versus parameters of the operation receiving it.
image_reason: The entry image places the O passage and flared vessel together, with source-profile signs. This is clearer for the core contrast than the B close-up.
image_cannot_prove: The snapshot does not establish arbitrary glyph support, an editable recipe, usable level passage or a closed vessel bottom.
proposal: Proposed two-branch diagram from one O outline: fixed section along a straight route, and changing section scale along another route. Keep source and route colours distinct; explicitly label the passage sill and the vessel's open end.
flags: A bounded learner edit host remains to be selected.
Do not infer branching connectivity between B's separate wells.
This exploration need not teach font extraction, triangulation or general topology.

student_action: Measure a closed polygon by adding neighbour distances, then change the acceptance tolerance while keeping the polygon fixed.
visible_consequence: The running total includes the closing edge; the same shape can pass or fail a different stated requirement.
useful_contrast: Changed construction versus changed decision; accumulated length difference versus maximum visible gap.
image_reason: The selected low-sided ring and its nested comparisons are much more legible than the aerial overview. The control readout is partly cropped.
image_cannot_prove: Perspective cannot measure approximation error, show a completed running total, or establish learner performance or portal transport.
proposal: Proposed planar polygon inset with consecutive edges highlighted into a numeric sum, ending with the closing edge. Show one fixed gap with two tolerances and different true/false results. Label the gap as a perimeter difference, not distance from polygon to circle.
flags: Use the supplied circumference reference; its formula is not a new trigonometry lesson.
Passing tolerance does not assert accessible passage, good art or a frame-rate guarantee.

student_action: Arrange three familiar bodies from a position list; change one entry and explain which body moves.
visible_consequence: One placement changes while the local vertices and other bodies retain their values.
useful_contrast: A list of position values and a list of created body references; arranging objects versus changing their geometry.
image_reason: The court gives a clear arrangement of forms and space without pretending to be the reduced three-pyramid study.
image_cannot_prove: The court's geometry does not reveal a loop or establish that its materials, collisions and positions are those of the companion study.
proposal: Proposed plan-view comparison with three numbered footprints: one changed Vector3 entry moves only the middle footprint. Keep the same shape silhouettes in both panels. A small list-to-reference correspondence can make instance creation legible without adding another room.
flags: Do not turn the critical Dürer encounter into a mandatory coding checkpoint.
Unfamiliar scale operations remain supplied until Transformation.
The authored-class foundation belongs later; here the learner instantiates a supplied builder.
